title: Percentage and Its Applications — Class 10 NIOS Mathematics
subject: Mathematics

slides.title: Percentage and Its Applications
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome students. Percent means 'per hundred' — a universal yardstick that drives commercial mathematics.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Convert between fractions, decimals and percents.
Apply x % of A and successive percentage changes.
Solve profit / loss / discount problems on CP and MP.
Compare yearly, half-yearly and quarterly compounding.
slides.speaker_notes: Read each; ask which seems hardest.

slides.title: Percent — three forms
slides.speaker_notes: Drill the conversions until they become automatic.

slides.title: Percentage of a quantity
slides.speaker_notes: Two formulas to memorise; both are about ratios.

slides.title: Increase and decrease percent
bullets: New after p % increase: A · (1 + p/100).
New after p % decrease: A · (1 − p/100).
Successive p % then q %: total = (1 + p/100)(1 + q/100).
Net % = p + q + pq/100 (NOT p + q).

slides.title: Successive 20 % and 25 % discounts
bullets: Lesson: successive % use multiplication, not addition.
slides.speaker_notes: Show both approaches; let students see the consistency.

slides.title: Profit and loss
bullets: CP = cost price; SP = selling price.
slides.speaker_notes: The 'on CP' rule is the chapter's biggest pitfall.

slides.title: Discount
bullets: MP = marked price; SP after discount.
Discount % is on MP (not on CP).
Combined with markup: MP = CP · (1 + markup%/100); SP = MP · (1 − d/100).

slides.title: Worked example: profit-and-discount combined
bullets: MP marked 30 % above CP; 10 % discount given.
Markup ≠ profit when there's a discount.
slides.speaker_notes: Highlight: actual profit % depends on BOTH markup and discount.

slides.title: Simple interest
bullets: Amount A = P + SI = P(1 + rt/100).
Each year you owe r % of the ORIGINAL principal.
Re-arrangements: P = SI·100/(rt); r = SI·100/(Pt); t = SI·100/(Pr).

slides.title: Compound interest — yearly
bullets: Each period, interest is added to principal.
slides.speaker_notes: Compare CI = 662 vs SI = 600 on the board.

slides.title: Sub-annual compounding
slides.speaker_notes: Demonstrate that increasing n raises the amount.

slides.title: You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 2. After two 10 % discounts, what's the equivalent single discount?
4. SI on ₹2500 at 6 % p.a. for 2 years.
slides.speaker_notes: Walk the room; address common slips.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q1. 60 % as a fraction in lowest terms?
Q3. Profit % is on CP or SP?
Q4. Discount % is on CP or MP?
slides.speaker_notes: Address the question with the most disagreement.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: % = per hundred. Three forms of one number.
Successive % multiply; (p + q + pq/100) is the net change.
Profit / loss % on CP. Discount % on MP.
